DATING APP CRIMES

By: Latashia Naidoo | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Looking for love online has led some dating app users down a path of blackmail, assault, and a extortion.

Unique Selling Point:
It’s a 21st century crime that targets dating app users.

Summary:
In recent years, users of popular dating apps, Tinder and Grindr, have reported falling victim to scams related to catfishing, extortion, harassment, assault, sextortion, and in some cases, even rape.

The global issue seems to have embedded itself in South African dating culture of late, where gay users of Grindr - a notorious ‘hookup’ app - have repeatedly fallen prey to assault and extortion - crimes which the police have largely failed to remedy.

Similarly, there have been a number accounts of abuse off Tinder - by primarily heterosexual users.

But some victims claim they’ve been unable to seek any support from authorities to solve these crimes, whilst receiving no responses from the app developers themselves.

Yet despite these online dangers and the very real consequences of anonymous connections, these apps have continued to grow in popularity.

We explore the stories of victims who have fallen prey to unscrupulous and violent criminals who’ve exploited these apps for nefarious gain; speak to experts about the psychological aspects of online dating and how dating apps have reshaped our romantic and sexual connections; and explore the elements of online dating that’s fraught with dangers and deception.


Further information:
We also speak to a woman who perpetuates these types of crimes on unsuspecting users on Tinder.

Press Release:


Cyber Cruelty

He was a young man looking for an exciting rendezvous with a new lover, and there seemed
no better place than the dating app Grindr, to find a like-minded companion. But it wasn’t a love match that he found. Within minutes of meeting his date, he knew something was wrong. What followed next was a terrifying ordeal of beatings,
torment and robbery. It’s a worrying trend because opportunistic criminals have moved in, catfishing, blackmailing and extorting money from users of dating apps. Those who’ve fallen victim to these crimes say they’ve received little support from police to solve these crimes and the app developers aren’t taking responsibility. In a special two part report, Carte Blanche investigates.


Producers:
Latashia Naidoo & Hein Kaizer | Presenter: Bongani Bingwa

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 10 May 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Cyber Cruelty He was a young man looking for an exciting rendezvous with a new lover, and there seemed no better place than the dating app Grindr, to find a like-minded companion. But it wasn’t a love match that he found. Within minutes of meeting his date, he knew something was wrong. What followed next was a terrifying ordeal of beatings, torment and robbery. It’s a worrying trend because opportunistic criminals have moved in, catfishing, blackmailing and extorting money from users of dating apps. Those who’ve fallen victim to these crimes say they’ve received little support from police to solve these crimes and the app developers aren’t taking responsibility. In a special two part report, Carte Blanche investigates. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Looking for love online has led some dating app users down a path of blackmail, assault, and a extortion.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: It’s a 21st century crime that targets dating app users.
metadata.Summary: In recent years, users of popular dating apps, Tinder and Grindr, have reported falling victim to scams related to catfishing, extortion, harassment, assault, sextortion, and in some cases, even rape. The global issue seems to have embedded itself in South African dating culture of late, where gay users of Grindr - a notorious ‘hookup’ app - have repeatedly fallen prey to assault and extortion - crimes which the police have largely failed to remedy. Similarly, there have been a number accounts of abuse off Tinder - by primarily heterosexual users. But some victims claim they’ve been unable to seek any support from authorities to solve these crimes, whilst receiving no responses from the app developers themselves. Yet despite these online dangers and the very real consequences of anonymous connections, these apps have continued to grow in popularity. We explore the stories of victims who have fallen prey to unscrupulous and violent criminals who’ve exploited these apps for nefarious gain; speak to experts about the psychological aspects of online dating and how dating apps have reshaped our romantic and sexual connections; and explore the elements of online dating that’s fraught with dangers and deception.
metadata.Further information: We also speak to a woman who perpetuates these types of crimes on unsuspecting users on Tinder.
